summary.headline: Asian Energy FY26 revenue rose 70% to INR791 crore, but Q4 missed previously guided numbers on West Asia-linked execution delays.
summary.overview: FY26 revenue from operations was INR791 crore (up 70% YoY) with EBITDA of INR99 crore (12.5% margin) and adjusted PAT of INR60.6 crore after a INR9 crore exceptional item tied to the Kuiper acquisition. Q4 revenue was INR338 crore (up 57%) and EBITDA INR49 crore (14.6% margin), but management said the company could not fully meet previously communicated FY26 guidance because supply-chain disruption from the West Asia conflict and client-side delays pushed revenue recognition into FY27. Management framed the shortfall as timing rather than lost revenue, and guided FY27 standalone growth of 30-40% with Kuiper revenue of USD 60-65 million. The Oilmax merger has SEBI approval, with the NCLT shareholder meeting in June 2026 and completion expected September or October 2026.

segments.name: Oil and Gas (Integrated Oil and Gas Services)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR633 crore with profit INR102 crore; Q4 revenue INR256 crore with profit INR42 crore. Management called performance steady, supported by execution, though part of Q4 revenue slipped into FY27.

segments.name: Minerals
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR158 crore and profit INR32 crore; Q4 revenue INR82 crore and profit INR18 crore. Management called it a key growth driver and said it is L1 in one minerals infrastructure tender.

segments.name: Kuiper (international manpower and O&M)
segments.commentary: Current annualised run rate of about INR530-540 crore per the analyst's question; management guided FY27 full-year top line of USD 60-65 million and EBITDA margin of about 7% in FY26, targeted to rise 100-200 bps.

segments.name: Oilmax (oilfield ownership)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue similar to FY25 (analyst cited about INR115-130 crore; management did not confirm the figure). Long-term guidance INR800-900 crore revenue in FY29-FY30; management gave no FY27/FY28 number.

guidance_outlook: FY27 standalone revenue growth of 30-40%; about 90-95% of this is covered by the existing order book and the L1 tender, per management.
FY27 Kuiper full-year top line of USD 60-65 million; Kuiper scale target of about USD 100 million by FY29 with 11-12% EBITDA margin.
Standalone EBITDA margin (about 16% in FY26) to rise 100-200 bps in FY27; consolidated EBITDA margin expected at 12-13%.
Standalone services business CAGR of 25-30% beyond FY27 (2-3 year view), per management.
Oilmax revenue INR800-900 crore targeted in FY29-FY30; Indrora and Mevad to reach about 1,000 BOPD in FY27 and 1,500 BOPD in the following 2-3 years.
FY29 PAT guidance of INR450-500 crore from the earlier AGM presentation reiterated as broadly unchanged. Dividend proposed at INR1.25 per share.
risks_watch: Q4 execution slippage: deferred revenue must be recognised in FY27, and FY27 guidance depends on that timing.
Duarmara testing outcome and production start date remain unconfirmed; it is the largest Oilmax asset by peak production, and the company gave no firm date.
Oilmax merger: NCLT meeting June 2026, completion targeted September or October 2026; integration and governance structure still being finalised.
West Asia conflict: disruption to supply chains, client delays, and Kuiper exposure through Qatar.
New business assumptions: coal gasification is at evaluation stage without in-house technology; the FY28+ growth rate relies on tenders not yet awarded (ONGC and others).
Consolidated and FY26 figures: the Oilmax revenue and PAT figures discussed on the call were not fully reconciled; management said Oilmax PAT margin is not comparable due to ESOPs.

qa_highlights.question: What was Oilmax revenue in FY26 and what can be expected in FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 Oilmax revenue similar to FY25; management gave INR800-900 crore for FY29-FY30 and no exact FY27/FY28 guidance. Margins not comparable due to ESOP grants.

qa_highlights.question: Status of Duarmara field, reasons for delay and production start?
qa_highlights.answer: Non-operator; operator Antelopus Selan found oil and gas shows, testing is tighter and ongoing with a workover rig. No date committed; a tentative date expected within about a month.

qa_highlights.question: Gasification capability and coal handling supply chain risks?
qa_highlights.answer: No in-house gasification know-how; in evaluation stage with technology partners under discussion. Coal handling equipment is largely domestically sourced, so no material challenge.

qa_highlights.question: Kuiper exposure to geopolitical tensions?
qa_highlights.answer: Brief disruption in Qatar in March; clients have remobilised and operations are almost normal. Kuiper also active in Southeast Asia and Africa.

qa_highlights.question: Capex plans for FY27 and FY28 and share of upstream spend?
qa_highlights.answer: No committed services or international capex. Only Indrora/Mevad infill drilling: about INR100 crore block outlay, INR50 crore Asian share. No large Oilmax capex commitment.

qa_highlights.question: How much FY27 standalone growth is covered by existing order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 90-95% of FY27 guidance comes from the INR1,750 crore order book and the L1 tender; no new orders assumed.

qa_highlights.question: Kuiper drivers to USD 100 million by FY29 and target margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth from new clients, new service lines and geographies; target EBITDA margin 11-12% versus about 7% currently. Standalone services CAGR of 25-30% beyond FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY29 PAT guidance of INR450-500 crore still valid?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said guidance is broadly unchanged, citing the plan and opportunities on hand.

qa_highlights.question: Mevad ramp-up status and funding for working capital and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Two new wells performed above expectations; rig mobilising for 6 more wells. Company is net zero debt with debt-to-equity virtually nil and banking support for working capital limits.

qa_highlights.question: How is Oilmax crude priced and how do higher prices affect cash flows?
qa_highlights.answer: Crude is sold to IOC under a formula linked to monthly average dated Brent; higher prices improve revenue.

capex_capacity: Management guided no committed capex for FY27 for the services business or international (Kuiper) expansion.
Only identified capex: additional wells at Indrora and Mevad; block-level outlay about INR100 crore over the next year, of which Asian's share is about INR50 crore.
Oilmax producing assets to ramp up without further capex; some blocks carry partner-funded capex.

Indrora and Mevad targeted at about 1,000 BOPD in FY27 and 1,500 BOPD in the following 2-3 years; mobilising a rig to drill 6 new wells at Mevad, with more than 200 barrels per day currently produced.
Duarmara: non-operator; operator Antelopus Selan running extended testing with a workover rig; no firm production start date, with an update expected in about a month.
Tiphuk production expected in coming months pending pipeline connectivity; Amguri to rise after connection to Numaligarh refinery and national grid over the next few months.
demand_pricing: FY27 order book about INR1,750 crore excluding taxes and excluding Kuiper; management said FY27 standalone guidance is about 90-95% covered by this order book plus the L1 tender.

Kuiper: major revenue is manpower supply via drilling rigs; diversifying into marine services, offshore construction and cable lay, plus EPC clients in Middle East and Southeast Asia; Nigeria and Africa under evaluation.
West Asia disruption in March affected Kuiper operations in Qatar only; management said most clients have remobilised and operations are near normal.
Mevad crude sold to Indian Oil Corporation under a contract priced on monthly average dated Brent, so higher crude prices raise revenue per barrel.
Minerals: L1 in one minerals infrastructure tender; pipeline spans coal gasification handling, critical minerals bulk material handling and ore-processing plant operations.
Oil and gas pipeline: management cited ONGC tenders for integrated field development (Vedanta model) and 3 bids under discovered small field round 4.
key_quotes: So the information we have got from them is that the well was drilled last year, as you correctly pointed out.
It's difficult for me to commit to a date to you today.
this is largely a timing-related impact rather than a loss of revenue and the deferred revenue are expected to recognise in FY '27 over the coming quarters
So, we do see a decent pipeline to keep us going for the next few years for the targeted growth rate.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the long-term outlook and policy tailwinds, but cautious and non-committal on near-term specifics: Duarmara timing, Oilmax FY27/FY28 numbers and gasification entry were left open. Management was openly candid that Q4 revenue slipped due to West Asia supply-chain and client delays.

adds.what: Additional wells at Indrora and Mevad; block-level outlay ~INR100 crore over next year (Asian share ~INR50 crore)
Rig mobilising to drill 6 new wells at Mevad (Indrora/Mevad targeted ~1,000 BOPD by FY27)
Amguri output rise after connection to Numaligarh refinery and national grid

growth.why: FY27 standalone revenue growth guided at 30-40% (midpoint 35%), with management saying ~90-95% is covered by an INR1,750 crore ex-Kuiper order book plus an L1 tender; Kuiper FY27 top line USD 60-65 million, but no committed services or international capex and Oilmax/well additions are small and timed over 1-4 quarters.
